entities.summary: Karl-Gustav Sauberzweig was a German Army Oberst (colonel) who transferred to the Waffen-SS during World War II and commanded the 13th Waffen Mountain Division of the SS Handschar in 1943–1944, and the IX Waffen Mountain Corps of the SS (Croatian) in 1944–1945, reaching the rank of SS-Gruppenführer and Generalleutnant of the Waffen-SS. He returned to the Wehrmacht in January 1945 and was appointed as a Generalleutnant to command a corps within Army Group H in northern Germany. Faced with the prospect of being extradited to Yugoslavia to stand trial for war crimes, Sauberzweig committed suicide in Allied captivity in 1946.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a high-ranking officer in the Waffen-SS, Sauberzweig played a significant role in the Eastern Front during World War II, leading units that committed atrocities against Soviet civilians and prisoners of war. His actions contributed to the suffering of thousands, making him a figure of historical significance.
